problem: Goal-conditioned visual navigation methods (ViNT, NoMaD, NaviBridger) mostly improve the policy head or diffusion action generation, while still using ImageNet-style CNN encoders with average pooling or self-attention for temporal fusion. This blurs fine-grained spatial structure and motion cues.
motivation: Blurred features cause oscillation, stalls and collisions in deployment, and hurt progress (temporal-distance) estimation. A t-SNE of NoMaD embeddings shows near- and far-from-goal states entangled, which suggests the representation itself, not the decision head, is the bottleneck.
key_idea: Replace pooling-based encoding with a spatio-temporal fusion encoder: a dynamic axial vision-GNN aggregates spatial structure within each frame, and a hybrid temporal shift plus multi-resolution difference-aware convolution models motion across frames, feeding a diffusion action head and a temporal-distance head.
insight: Improving the visual representation alone, with the same kind of diffusion policy head, yields large gains in success and collisions, especially on long-horizon and adaptation tasks. In the long-horizon ablation, removing temporal fusion drops success from 98% to 38%, and removing spatial aggregation drops it to 88%, so temporal fusion matters most and the two parts are complementary. Vanilla NoMaD with history often does worse than NoMaD-0 (current frame only), showing that naive average-pooling temporal fusion can hurt.
method: Shared CNN feature extraction: encodes each observation frame and the goal image into feature maps, which are treated as graph nodes
Dynamic axial graph construction: nodes connect along horizontal/vertical axes via circular shifts at multiple strides, with soft edge weights exp(-L1 distance/tau), tau=0.1, and no kNN search

Graph feature aggregation: depthwise-conv positional encoding, multi-scale contrast enhancement (weighted shifted residuals, max over H/W directions, K_list=[8,4,2]), then a 1x1 conv residual transform

Hybrid temporal shift module: channels are split into forward, backward, bidirectional and residual groups (rho=0.125) and shifted along time, followed by a depthwise 3x1x1 plus pointwise Conv3D and a residual connection

Dynamic multi-resolution contrast: at each scale, adaptive pooling, half-size circular roll, upsampling and subtraction give residuals, which a cosine-similarity mask filters and learnable beta_k weights sum into X_diff
Contrast-aware fusion: X_tsm and X_diff are concatenated and fused by a 1x1x1 Conv3D into the context c_T
Dual heads and joint training: a diffusion policy (masked MSE noise-prediction loss) plus a temporal-distance MSE regressor, with loss alpha*L_dist+(1-alpha)*L_diff, alpha=0.0001

setting.backbone: STRNet spatio-temporal encoder (CNN + dynamic axial GNN + temporal shift/contrast) with diffusion policy head, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Unified dataset of RECON, SCAND, GoStanford and SACSoN real-robot trajectories (image sequences with positions), shared with all baselines
setting.observation: monocular RGB image sequence plus goal image
setting.action_space: waypoint/action sequences from a diffusion policy (continuous)
setting.simulator: 2D-3D-S, Citysim, GRScenes (Isaac-based GRUtopia); plus real world

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks; results are on custom simulation tasks (2D-3D-S, Citysim, GRScenes). Real-world results are qualitative only. GRScenes SR is printed as a fraction even though the header says %.
results: STRNet gets 100% success in the 2D-3D-S indoor basic and adaptation tasks and 100%/92% on Citysim basic/adaptation. On Citysim adaptation the strongest baseline is ViNT at 66%. On the long-horizon 2D-3D-S task STRNet reaches 98% versus 68% for ViNT and 30% for NoMaD. On GRScenes SR is 0.79 versus 0.72 for NaviBridger, and under noisy subgoals it reaches 84% versus 76% for NaviBridger.
limitations: Evaluated on custom simulated tasks with only small trial counts (about 50 repeats, 10 per path on GRScenes); real-world evidence is qualitative only
Only RGB is used, with no depth, lidar or language input and no explicit memory
FLOPs and latency are slightly higher than NoMaD (3.56M vs 1.70M FLOPs; 36.52 ms vs 36.06 ms)
